messages:
maya: Seeing a sudden pile of Pending GPU pods in ap-southeast1c since ~03:00 UTC. Eviction counts spiked and a bunch of tiny pods are being bounced. cc @devin @sam :eyes:

devin: Yup, noticed it as well. Eviction log shows a taint applied to 4 nodes in rack ap-southeast1c: `gpu-maint:NoSchedule` — timestamps align with yesterday's rollout window.

sam: I ran the taint rollout yesterday but targeted ap-southeast1b only. Did the label-syncer expand racks? Noted some rack labels were recently mass-updated.

maya: Possible. Current problem is fragmentation + preempt churn: many pods are tiny (0.1-0.5 GPU) so they spread and then get evicted -> back to pending and we keep launching more warm nodes. Cost and slot churn going up.

devin: Quick data: eviction rate ~6/min for that pool, pending queue doubled. `kubectl get nodes -l rack=ap-southeast1c -o wide` shows 4 nodes tainted and 2 healthy but saturated.

leyla: If we untaint immediately, will we risk letting the maintenance land mid-inference? Also untainting will reduce evicts but could mask whatever the underlying kernel/drivers issue was.

sam: Agreed. Two options: rollback taint (fast, reduces churn), or scale warm-pool by +2-3 to absorb requeues while we investigate. Rollback buys time but we should verify the maintenance intent.

infra-sre: We have 6 spare GPUs available in the region but cold spin ~6m. Warm-pool increase (ephemeral reserved) possible: cost ~ $1.20/hr per GPU. Rough delta: 3 GPUs -> ~$3.6/hr. Current unit-cost already up because of requeues.

devin: I can do a targeted rollback on the 4 nodes to stop the eviction loop, then reapply taints with a safer canary script that checks `k8s-drainable` and `gpu-allocs` thresholds. Command I'll run:

```
kubectl taint nodes node-apse1c-0{2,3,4,5} gpu-maint:NoSchedule-  # remove taint
# then reapply via script with checks
```

maya: Doing the rollback now. Will tail `kubelet` + eviction controller for 10m.

ops-bot: Incident bot: Eviction alert (ap-southeast1c GPU pool) acknowledged by devin at 03:18 UTC. Autoscaler paused for region to reduce thundering.

maya: Rollback applied to nodes 02,03,04,05. Pending queue started to drain within ~90s for a subset. Still monitoring for any kernel offlines.

sam: Nice. After things stabilize we should: 1) audit the label-syncer run that touched racks 2) add a canary gate to taint rollout that checks `pending/gpu` <= 10 and `eviction_rate` < 1/min 3) add a cost-hedge alert to notify when warm pool scale triggers >2x baseline.

leyla: Can we add a short-lived guard that prevents automated taints from touching racks with >60% frag? That would prevent this packing-collapse.

infra-sre: Ack. I'll open a quick runbook PR: `rollback + verify + safe-reapply` and add cost estimate and warm-pool ops. Will follow up with quotas and approve small warm bump if needed.

devin: Leaving autoscaler paused until we confirm steady-state. If anyone sees re-evict spikes ping `#eng-oncall` and I'll re-evaluate.

maya: Thanks all. Postmortem item: why did the syncer include ap-southeast1c? Also check driver update tags on those tainted nodes.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: Eviction rate back below threshold. Logged as incident 2026-03-23-apse1c-evict-loop. :white_check_mark:
